 **PHILIPPINE JUNIOR DATA SCIENCE CHALLENGE 2026**

| PAGE 1 | EVENT SYNOPSIS |
| :---- | :---- |

|  | ABOUT THE EVENT |  |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |

The Philippine Junior Data Science Challenge (PJDSC) 2026, organized by the UP Data Science Society (UP DSSoc), is a nationwide data science event open to all interested students currently in senior high school or university. PJDSC 2026 consists of talks, workshops, an initial proposal submission, and a data science project, all of which aim to provide an avenue for students to learn, apply, and develop data skills in a competitive setting.

|  | WHAT IS DATA SCIENCE? |  |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |

Data science is a multidisciplinary field that combines statistics, mathematics, and computer science to extract meaningful insights from data. It involves collecting, analyzing, and interpreting large volumes of data to uncover patterns, make predictions, and inform decision-making. Data scientists use various tools and techniques, including machine learning algorithms and data visualization, to turn raw data into actionable insights. By applying these methods, they help organizations solve complex problems, optimize processes, and drive innovation.

In this competition, participants will be formulating a project that demonstrates how data science can be applied to address real-world challenges in public health analytics.

| PAGE 2 | THEME INTRODUCTION |
| :---- | :---- |

|  | THEME & TITLE |  |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |

This year’s PJDSC focuses on Public Health Analytics with the theme: “Trace the Pattern, Target the Cure: Advancing Public Health Through Data Science”

|  | CHALLENGE STATEMENT |  |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |

Communities across the Philippines face complex public health challenges that require timely, effective, and accessible solutions. From monitoring disease outbreaks and predicting health risks to improving healthcare delivery and resource distribution, data plays an increasingly important role in shaping public health decisions. However, transforming diverse health datasets into meaningful insights and actionable strategies remains a challenge.

How can data analytics and innovative approaches be leveraged to develop practical solutions that improve disease prevention, support early intervention, strengthen healthcare systems, and promote healthier communities?

| PAGE 3 & 4 | EVENT MECHANICS |
| :---- | :---- |

	The competition is open to teams of three to five members, with a maximum of 40 teams accepted on a first-come, first-served basis. To participate, each team must first submit an initial proposal aligned with the competition’s theme. Following this submission, participants will engage in a curated series of talks and workshops designed to help them refine their concepts and enhance their technical execution. 

Teams will then submit a final proposal package, consisting of a polished slide deck, source code, and a recorded demo video. These will be evaluated during the Project-Based Elimination Round. The top ten teams will advance to receive mentorship and further development support, culminating in a live presentation of their final working solutions at the face-to-face Culminating Event.

|  | REGISTRATION |  |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |

![][image1]

1. The competition is open to teams composed of 3 to 5 members. Each member must be at least a senior high school student or a tertiary student from a school or university in the Philippines. The members need not be from the same university or school.   
2. Registration will be on a first-come, first-served basis based on the validity of submissions and the time of submission limited to a total of 40 teams.  
3. A demographic quota (National Capital Region, Luzon, Visayas, Mindanao; 5 per each) will be implemented for the early registration. An open demographic, first-come, first-served basis will be open for the Regular Registration Period.   
   1. Teams may choose to represent a region on the conditions that: (1) at least one of the team members is from the chosen region, (2) the university that at least one of the team members is from the chosen region.   
   2. Quota slots may be forfeited by the organizers if found non-eligible for the chosen region for the purpose of bypassing the regional requirements.  
4. Early registration will be open from September 21, 2026, 5:00 PM to September 25, 2026, 11:59 PM. Regular registration will follow from September 28, 2026, 5:00 PM to September 30, 2026, 11:59 PM. Each team must complete their registration within the designated period and upload the required documents through the provided Google Form: *reg link here when available*   
5. There will be a registration fee for each team member of 300.00 pesos for early registrants and 350.00 pesos for late registrants. A strict no refund policy is enforced.  
6. Members of the UP Data Science Society may also compete as long as they are not Executive Board (EB) members, Vice-Directors (VD), and PJDSC 2026 managing members of the organization.

Registration Link:  \[[tinyurl.com/pjdsc2026earlybird](https://tinyurl.com/pjdsc2026earlybird)\]

|  | COMPETITION FLOW |  |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |

|  | ELIMINATION ROUND |  |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |

1) ### **Concept Proposal Submission**

1. Each team must submit a PDF of their initial concept proposal based on the competition theme.   
2. Written proposals are limited to a maximum of five (5) pages, excluding the title page. The five-page limit includes all references and appendices. Teams should ensure their outputs include the ***background, problem statement, objectives, scope, and methodology*** of their proposal. The proposal template can be accessed through this [link](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSc0Z2ENcJbGnPfzAfO9EQvhO9rdRw5xlKJ6b4m1UkcxaM_5FA/viewform?usp=header) \[[https://bit.ly/pjdsc2026pptemplate](https://bit.ly/pjdsc2026pptemplate)\]  
3. Submissions for the initial concept proposal will open at the official event launch on October 10, 2026, 12:00 AM, and will close on October 12, 2026, 11:59 PM. Teams may begin preparing their proposals in advance and submit them through this link once available: [bit.ly/pjdsc2026ConceptProposalSubmission](http://bit.ly/pjdsc2026ConceptProposalSubmission)   
4. Topics from the theme include but are not limited to: Disease Surveillance and Outbreak Monitoring, Disease Risk Prediction and Early Detection, Epidemiological Modeling and Transmission Analysis, Healthcare Resource Planning and Optimization, Healthcare Access and Service Delivery, Community Health Assessment and Intervention, Environmental Health and Risk Analysis, Health Behavior and Population Trends, Digital Health Systems and Applications, and Public Health Communication and Decision Support.   
5. The concept proposals should include the identification of at least one problem in the field of public health analytics and at least one proposed solution or method of mitigating and addressing any of the identified problems.  
6. The solutions may be in the form of a web application, mobile app, dashboard, or **any usable product**.  
7. To be eligible for the final project submission round, each team must submit a complete initial proposal containing all required components ***and have at least one representative attend the official event launch***. Only teams that meet both requirements will be allowed to participate in the workshops and collaboration sessions.

2) ### **Project Development Stage**

1. After the initial proposal submission, teams will enter the development phase, during which they are expected to refine their project through curated workshops and talks.   
2. Each final proposal must include an updated slide deck (PDF), a recorded project demonstration video, and a link to the complete code repository.   
3. Slide decks are strictly limited to a maximum of twenty (20) slides, including the title slide, references, and appendices. The recorded video presentation must not exceed three (3) minutes in length. Exceeding either limit will incur a deduction based on the extent of non-compliance: 1 point for every 1–2 slides beyond the 20-slide limit, and 1 point for every 15 seconds beyond the 3-minute limit, up to a maximum of 10 points per requirement.  
4. Final projects must be submitted on or before October 24, 2026, 11:59 PM through this link: [bit.ly/pjdsc2026FinalProjectSubmission](http://bit.ly/pjdsc2026FinalProjectSubmission)   
5. The projects must include and will be judged with the following criteria:  
1. ***Project Rationale and Design** – Problem Statement and Motivation; Data Sources and Acquisition; Methodology and Approach*  
2. ***Execution and Impact** – Findings and Analysis; Challenges and Mitigation Strategies; Future Directions and Real-World Application*  
3. ***Code Repository** – Code Structure and Documentation; Functional Execution and Reproducibility; Dependencies and Data Management*  
4. ***Demonstration Video** – Communication Quality and Clarity; Technical Content and Functional Showcase; Enhancement of Audience Comprehension*  
5. ***Technical Rigor and Innovation** – Validity and Appropriateness of Techniques; Novelty and Creativity; Analytical Depth*  
6. ***Sources** – Reliable, up-to-date, APA 7th Edition*  
6. The Top 10 teams will be selected based on the above criteria and will be announced on November 4, 2026, via PJDSC’s official social media channels and direct email notification.

|  | EVENT CULMINATION |  |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |

1) ### **Advanced Workshop**

1. A series of online workshops will be conducted on November 7, 2026, primarily designed for the Top 10 teams advancing to the final round.  
2. The workshop will cover key data science concepts and techniques relevant to the development and refinement of the finalists' projects.  
3. Each finalist team will be assigned a mentor for a dedicated mentorship session afterward to provide tailored guidance and support.  
4. Non-qualifying teams are welcome to attend the workshop, but will not be eligible to participate in the mentorship sessions.

2) ### **Final Round**

1. Finalist teams will present their final working project or product through a live, interactive demonstration of their prototype or solution on November 14, 2026, in Quezon City.  
2. Each team is required to deliver a stage presentation lasting ten (10) minutes, followed by a ten (10)-minute Q\&A segment with the panel of judges. The presentation time limit will be strictly enforced. Teams that reach the ten (10)-minute limit will be immediately stopped, and no additional presentation time will be permitted.   
3. The Finalist Teams will be judged with the following criteria:  
   1. ***Demonstrated Functionality & Technical Robustness** – Technical Execution and Performance; Code Quality and Reproducibility*  
   2. ***Impact and Real-World Applicability** – Tangible Impact; Scalability and Deployment; Sustainability*  
   3. ***User Experience & Design** – Accessibility and Intuitiveness; Interaction Design; Output Clarity and Insight Communication*  
   4. ***Presentation & Communication** – Presentation Quality and Engagement; Q\&A Competence*  
   5. ***Sources** – Reliable, up-to-date, APA 7th Edition.*  
4. Each team shall be assigned a dedicated demonstration station in addition to their onstage presentation. The demonstration station is provided for exhibit and viewing purposes only and will not be included in the official evaluation or scoring of the competition.  
5. The project in its entirety, including the code and datasets, will be featured on the UP Data Science Society’s official GitHub page with proper citation given to each contributing team member. Selected project outputs may also be featured on the organization’s official social media platforms for promotional and informational purposes. By participating in the competition, teams acknowledge and consent to the publication of their submitted works on these platforms.  
   *We at UP Data Science believe that sharing your work with the public is crucial for driving progress and innovation. By making your insights accessible, you not only enhance your impact and visibility but also inspire collaboration and contribute to the broader community. Together, we can achieve more by sharing our knowledge.*

| PAGE 6 | FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS |
| :---- | :---- |

1. I am not from Computer Science, Statistics, Engineering, or any degree program directly related to Data Science. Am I still allowed to register?  
- *The competition is open to all undergraduates from any university with no restrictions on degree programs.*  
2. I’m an undergraduate but currently on LOA, can I still participate?  
- *Yes, you may still participate if you are an undergraduate who is currently on Leave of Absence.*  
3. Do I need to have any programming experience to join the competition?  
- *It is not a requirement, but it would help. We will hold a workshop with learning sessions to be able to widen your knowledge in data science but most of the programming aspect is left for you to learn.*  
4. What programming language are we allowed to use?  
- *You are allowed to use anything as long as you are able to successfully formulate your proposed data science solutions.*  
5. Can our team have members from different universities and regions?  
- *Yes. You are free to team up with members from all over the Philippines as long as they meet the criteria for joining.*  
6. Where will the Hybrid/Face-to-face events take place?  
- *The venue for the hybrid/face-to-face events will be in Metro Manila, with the exact location to be determined. Updates will be announced on the Philippine Junior Data Science Challenge Facebook page.*  
7. What if one of our team members drops out during the event?  
- *It is okay as long as you still have at least 3 members. However, if you do not meet the minimum number of members, you will need to find a replacement member.*  
8. Where will the hybrid or face-to-face events be held?  
- *The venue will be in **Metro Manila**, with the exact location to be determined. Please refer to our official Facebook page for the latest updates and announcements.*  
9. Can non-finalist participants attend the final round or culminating event?  
- *Depending on the attendance limit of the culminating event, non-finalist participants are welcome to attend the final culminating event as visitors. They may explore the booths of finalist teams, as well as those of event sponsors and partners for networking and engagement opportunities.* 

| PAGE 6 | ORGANIZER INFORMATION |
| :---- | :---- |

|  | ABOUT THE ORGANIZER |  |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |

Founded in 2020, UP Data Science Society (UP DSSoc) is the first data science organization at the University of the Philippines (UP). The organization aims to provide an environment for aspiring data scientists to engage in insightful data science discussions and to hone their skills, regardless of skill level, through workshops and other opportunities. UP DSSoc also envisions itself as a multidisciplinary organization that equips and empowers members to use data science to produce data-driven solutions for social good, aligning both internal and external events to contribute to the advancement of communities at large. The work and activities held in UP DSSoc revolve around the organization's core values of Purposeful Learning, Community for Innovation, and Utak at Puso.

1) ### **Our Vision**

A multidisciplinary organization whose members contribute to society through innovative solutions to community problems using Data Science, and help responsibly develop the field of Data Science in the country.

2) ### **Our Mission**

To provide an avenue for Data Science enthusiasts of UP Diliman to safely share ideas and experiences, hone their skills, and collaborate to build socially relevant and impactful projects while promoting data science and its real-life applications.
